_note: Ground truth for the rubric. The first 25 were labelled 2026-09-02 and the next 75 on 2026-09-08, both from digest/prompts/rubric.md, both by Claude rather than by the lens's owner: they are a considered reading of the rubric, not the owner's own judgement, and every model score in scripts/eval_rubric.py moves when a label is corrected. Items are drawn from real runs over 2026-08-25 to 2026-09-04 across 19 feeds, sampled at random with a per-source cap so no one feed dominates — deliberately NOT sampled by the classifier's own fit score, which would bias the set toward the model's uncertainties. `kind` is the internal slot (core/adjacent/neither), not the lens's display word; a label keyed to a display word silently scores zero. Labels are keyed by item id; `title` is for reading. Thomas ruled on four boundary questions on 2026-09-08, after a second independent labelling by Fable disagreed on 16 items, always in the same direction. His answers: (1) something announced but not enacted — a pitch, a plan, a warning, an imminent ruling — DOES reach fit 2. (2) an analysis piece that names a mechanism but reports no event does NOT. (3) an event whose structural consequence is real but unstated DOES; the piece need not draw the consequence itself. (4) a first-in-35-years threshold is novelty, not fit. These are the owner's calls and outrank either rater's reading. On 2026-09-08 Thomas added a geography rule to the lens: Africa and low-income and developing countries generally are off-lens on their own, and score normally only when a great power is a party to what changed (the Belt and Road being the exemplary case). Eight items were relabelled to fit 0 under it. Two nearby items were deliberately NOT relabelled and are the judgement calls to check: Abu Dhabi's M42 in Botswana, which is Gulf capital and so has a great power as a party, and the Iran-Oman Hormuz deal, which is a chokepoint regime rather than a domestic story.
